title.value: The Impact of Positional Encoding on Length Generalization in Transformers
title.justification: This value was chosen because it is explicitly specified as the paper's title by the authors.
title.quote: The Impact of Positional Encoding on Length Generalization in Transformers Amirhossein Kazemnejad1 , Inkit Padhi2 Karthikeyan Natesan Ramamurthy2 , Payel Das2 , Siva Reddy1,3,4

extractions.description: The paper conducts a systematic empirical study on the effect of different positional encoding methods on the length generalization performance of decoder-only Transformers. It evaluates various positional encoding approaches, including Absolute Position Embedding, T5's Relative PE, ALiBi, and Rotary, compared to Transformers without positional encoding. It finds that the commonly used positional encodings are not well-suited for length generalization, while Transformers without explicit positional encoding perform better. The study also explores theoretical aspects of positional encoding capabilities in Transformers.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on analyzing positional encodings in Transformers concerning their length generalization capabilities, without any explicit mention of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development themes.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Length generalization, the ability to generalize from small training context sizes to larger ones, is a critical challenge in the development of Transformer-based language models.

primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on technical aspects of machine learning models in terms of their ability to generalize over input lengths, common to language processing tasks, and does not relate to any specific Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development goals.
primary_category.quote: Our work suggests that explicit position encodings are not essential for decoder-only Transformers to generalize well to longer sequences.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper does not cover topics related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development, hence no secondary categories apply.
secondary_categories.quote: Our results show that: Most commonly used positional encoding methods, including ALiBi, Rotary, and APE, are ill-suited for length generalization in downstream tasks.

primary_sub_category.quote: We conduct a systematic study on the length generalization of decoder-only Transformers, popularized by the GPT-family of models.

secondary_sub_categories.quote: These techniques are architecture-independent and can be used with any PE method. However, it remains an open question whether these techniques, at least in regard to length generalization, render the choice of PE irrelevant.

applications.quote: We find that using no positional encoding is better than using explicit positional encodings.
